referees.quote: In my opinion, the work seems suitable for publication in Nature Communications. In the following, I give some specific comments.
I have a few queries, especially about the STM measurements (which I am well-equipped to evaluate), before I can make a decision about whether the paper should be accepted
I find that the manuscript is a bit weak in the interpretation part. Overall, I believe this work will be worth considering for publication in Nat. Comm. only after appropriate revisions.

note: First round is Version 0; the file shows no sign of a transfer from another journal, and no referee co-signs another's report. R1 judges the work suitable and asks for mostly presentational fixes plus more discussion, so minor revision. R2 withholds a decision and asks for new STM spectroscopy and phase analysis, and questions whether the effect is a CDW at all, so major revision. R3's level is a judgment call between minor and major. R3 asks for substantial new interpretation (the mechanism of the large displacement, why the CDW is absent in bulk) and a new title, so major revision. R3's comments are misnumbered in the original, with no item 2 and two items numbered 4.
